omitted.why: The request supplies no named vendor, verified shutdown notice, report, decision, statutory language, coalition letter, or attributed response to cite or quote.

claims.claim: Vendors closing connected-home cloud services often describe the decision as the retirement of an online service.
Connected-home cloud servers authenticate devices or users, coordinate operations, and relay commands.
Households commonly encounter or recognize the described connected-device reinstallation scenario.
Sales of connected appliances include nonphysical operational capabilities in addition to the physical hardware and power components.
The sale of a connected appliance includes a continuing ability to perform its advertised functions.
For cloud-dependent connected appliances, continuing vendor service is embedded in the product's operation.
Cloud services provide practical benefits for connected-home devices.
Cloud service can make remote access to connected-home devices more convenient.
Cloud service can simplify updates for connected-home devices.
Cloud service can connect devices across different networks, including access from outside the home.
Connected appliances can provide the identified cloud-supported benefits without being permanently dependent on the cloud for core operation.
Connected appliances can use cloud support for added capabilities without making the cloud a single point of failure.
Local operation protects the core functions of connected-home devices when vendor cloud service closes.
Publishing a connected device's protocols enables compatible software to replace a discontinued application.
Export tools preserve a connected device's settings and data after service or application discontinuation.
Releasing software or protocols, transferring service, and providing a long transition period each entail costs and security questions.
